newsitem.title: UK: Rolls says Trent 900 engine puts it ahead.
newsitem.headline: Rolls says Trent 900 engine puts it ahead.

text.p: Engine maker Rolls-Royce Plc said on Monday that the development of its Trent 900 aero engine put it ahead of U.S. rivals in the battle to supply the new class of "super jumbo" jets.

The Trent 900 engine was formally launched at the industry showcase -- the Farnborough International air show -- with Rolls Royce chairman Sir Ralph Robins telling a press conference that talks were already under way with potential buyers incuding British Airways Plc, Singapore Airlines and Australia's Quantas, all major long-haul operators.
U.S. commercial aerospace giant Boeing Co is leading a two-horse race to develop the next generation of high capacity jumbo jets with its proposed 747-600X and 747-500X.
It could be ready for service in 2000, while European rival be ready until 2003.

Robins said Rolls' 80,000-pounds thrust engine aimed to have certification for December 1999, ready for service with Boeing Co by 2000. The speed of its development should give it a headstart over rivals General Electric and United Technologies unit Pratt & Whitney of the U.S., he said.
The chairman said because the engine design was derived from earlier models, development costs were "very moderate" and more importantly "very predictable", making it a low risk enterprise.
Charles Cuddington, the Trent 900 project director, told the news confernce the engine "meets and exceeds all of Boeing's requirements" on range, noise levels and cost.

The Rolls Royce team said the engine also had a light weight which would be difficult to match. "Our weight advantage is going to be very, very tough to erode," Robins said. Rolls forecast 900 aircraft would be built which could use its Trent 900 engine, 800 in the passenger market and 100 in freight.
